deviations: Follower-to-follower separation in the 2 and 3 follower slice uses Run D's cooperative reciprocal velocity rule (separation_rule coop, decision D-123, made after the pre-registration), not the pre-registered pairwise 0.6 m stand-in guard.
The separation_rule local rows of the followers slice (the pre-registered 0.6 m stand-in guard) were added afterwards, for comparison only.
guard_activations now counts follower control steps where the coop rule changed the velocity; in the separation_rule local rows it counts pair-steps inside 0.6 m.
limits: Simulated only: no drone or radio hardware was used.
Link loss patterns are synthetic (named presets in sim/missions/presets.py), never measured.
Vehicle parameters are literature-derived (point mass, or the crazyflie-class physics profile).
Simulated only: target paths, radio delays, and link losses are synthetic.
Separation from the target uses the pre-registered stopping-buffer guard on the estimate (assumes 4 m/s^2 braking); the target takes no part in avoidance, so Run D's rule does not apply to it.
Slot assignment (linear_sum_assignment with a 1 s dwell) is a Run E rule; Run D's allocation is not used.

separation_rule coop (default, 2 or 3 followers): followers avoid each other with Run D's reciprocal velocity rule (sim.coop.avoidance.safe_velocity) on delivered, dead-reckoned telemetry, radius 0.35 m plus Run D's buffer from runs/d4-separation/buffer.json.  Run D tested it only on kinematic point masses with independent loss, so bursty presets and the physics adapter are outside that evidence; telemetry velocity is the simulated vehicle's own, without estimation noise.  guard_activations counts follower control steps where the rule changed the preferred velocity.
separation_rule local: pairwise 0.6 m follower-follower goal guard, a stand-in until Run D, kept for comparison; guard_activations counts pair-steps inside 0.6 m.
The jink path is softly mirrored inside [1,15] x [1,9], a Run E change.
missing_metrics: zone entry time (the mission logs tag_zone_enter events but exposes no zone-entry metric)
prediction: clean: straight and turn about 100 %, figure eight about 100 %, jinking 85 to 100 %. Delay up to 0.3 s barely matters at 0.5 m/s (lag v*d = 0.15 m is inside the 0.5 m wide zone ring) for recovery; naive loses a little on jinking at 0.5 s. iid_10: still high (default T = 0.3 s at 20 Hz fires about 0.07 times per hour at 10 %). iid_30: about 37 unnecessary landings per hour, so about 26 % of 30 s rounds end in a landing. Bursty presets are where tag fails: burst_10_0.5s triggers about 400 landings per hour, so most 30 s rounds end in a landing before the tag completes (predict tag success under 20 % with "default", recovered to 50 to 80 % by "calm"). Separation violations: 0 on clean; a few on jinking under bursts. Two and three followers: higher success on jinking (someone is in position) but more follower-follower guard activity; no gain when the limit is the landing failsafe (every follower sees the same bad radio). Physics adapter: same ordering, slightly lower success from the controller lag.
prediction_correction_2: 2. EXP-030 prediction for bursty presets: rounds end at the tag (about 5 s on easy classes), not at 30 s. With about 400 unnecessary landings per hour on burst_10_0.5s, the expected number in 5.3 s is 0.59, so P(no landing) is about e^-0.59 = 0.55. Corrected prediction: default policy tag success about 45 to 60 % on burst_10_0.5s for straight and turn, lower for figure eight and jinking (longer rounds); burst_30_0.5s about 15 to 30 %; "calm" (T = 1.0 s) raises both by 20 to 40 points.
